The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

As a Product Manager at Ramp, you will be responsible for the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Ramp’s international payments products. You will lead a core team of engineers and designers to build and scale global money movement capabilities that enable our customers to pay vendors, employees, and partners around the world. You’ll own a critical set of customer and business problems at the intersection of payments, compliance, risk, and FX — driving end-to-end product vision, strategy, and execution to power Ramp’s global expansion and meet ambitious company goals. Your scope will include:

  1. Cross-border payments & FX – Own the experience and infrastructure for sending and receiving international payments across currencies and geographies, including FX pricing, rate transparency, settlement speed, and reliability across multiple payment rails.

  2. Global partner ecosystem – Evaluate, integrate, and manage banking, FX, and local payment service partners to expand Ramp’s coverage, improve unit economics, and unlock new corridors and capabilities.

  3. Compliance & risk infrastructure – Partner with Legal, Compliance, and Risk to design scalable KYC/KYB, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, and regulatory frameworks that enable safe and compliant international money movement.

  4. New market expansion – Launch international capabilities in new geographies, navigating local regulations, licensing requirements, and operational constraints while delivering a seamless customer experience.

We’re looking for someone who can partner and collaborate across various internal teams, has a deep understanding of our customers and technology, and can deliver financial products to streamline complex business flows via a fantastic user experience.

What You'll Do

  • Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for international payments at Ramp

  • Drive high-velocity execution with a world-class team of engineers and designers, balancing principled intuition with data-driven decision making

  • Marry customer insights with technical possibilities, crafting intuitive user experiences that abstract away complexity

  • Help thousands of finance teams on Ramp more successfully manage their finances by expanding the capabilities of our product

  • Prototype rapidly using tools like Claude to accelerate the product development lifecycle and fast-forward to production-ready products.

  • Stay deeply plugged into AI research, industry trends, and emergent applications, filtering signal from noise and applying it creatively to Ramp’s product

What You Need

  • BA/BS in a technical or analytical field

  • Minimum 3 years product management experience

  • Strong customer empathy and design thinking

  • Fluency in data and how to make data-driven product decisions

  • Experience evaluating product decisions and prioritization trade-offs

  • Demonstrated ability to lead and influence small teams of engineers & designers toward a common goal

  • Ability to collaborate with multiple stakeholders and large cross-functional teams

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Passion for AI, shown through hands-on building, prototyping, or side projects, and staying current on research and tools.

  • Fluency with modern prototyping tools (e.g. Cursor, Bolt, Claude Code) and comfort with design/collaboration environments like Figma and Git.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Background in fast-paced, high-growth startup environments

  • Experience building payments products or products in regulated markets

  • Experience building products with a significant AI component, especially if leveraging LLMs.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

As the founding Channel Partner Manager for Canada, you will build the partner motion that helps Canadian businesses discover, evaluate, and adopt Ramp through trusted advisors and ecosystem partners.

This is a zero-to-one role. You will own the full partner lifecycle, from identifying and engaging Canadian accounting, advisory, private equity, and venture capital partners through signing, enablement, activation, and partner-sourced pipeline. Your early results will help determine how Ramp scales its Canadian channel motion.

You will work closely with Sales, Growth, Product, Engineering, and the broader Partnerships organization. The right person is a hands-on builder: equally comfortable opening a new relationship, running a partner meeting, solving an operational blocker, and turning early learnings into a repeatable playbook.

What You’ll Do

  • Build Ramp’s Canadian channel strategy and operating rhythm from the ground up.

  • Research, identify, source, qualify and sign net-new Canadian partners.

  • Create joint go-to-market and activation plans to grow the Canadian partner ecosystem.

  • Drive revenue for Ramp through generating referrals

  • Develop trusted relationships with decision-makers and operators inside partner orgs

  • Educate partners on Ramp’s Canadian capabilities, value prop and updates.

  • Own partner onboarding, activation, pipeline generation, and regular business reviews.

  • Work closely with the Canadian Sales team to advance partner-referred opportunities.

  • Partner with Product to surface recurring partner needs and inform the Canadian roadmap.

What You’ll Need

  • 5+ years of relevant experience, including 3+ years in partner sales, business development, channel partnerships, or a closely related role

  • High agency, urgency, and resilience

  • Proven track record of sourcing and managing partnerships

  • Self-starter mindset: you are comfortable getting in the weeds

  • Strong discovery and consultative-selling skills

  • Excellent written and verbal communication

  • Strong operating discipline and comfort using data to improve performance.

  • Proven ability to succeed in a fast-paced environment

  • Strong cross-functional judgment and a history of finding success across cross-functional work

  • Familiarity with the Canadian business and technology ecosystem

  • Strong comfort using AI tools to execute quality work, fast

  • Ability to travel to in-person events in Canada frequently

Nice to Have

  • Experience building a new partner motion, market, or vertical from an early stage.

  • Professional proficiency or native-level fluency in French

  • Presence in the Canadian accounting, advisory, private equity, venture capital, financial-services, or technology partner network

  • Familiarity with finance & accounting workflows and solutions

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Technical Consulting is Ramp's post-sales technical delivery team. When a finance org needs Ramp to work the way their business actually runs, this is the team that takes customers through that transformation, from complex accounting issues to integration errors to everything in between.

The Senior Manager, Technical Consulting, Strategic leads the team responsible for Ramp's largest and most strategic accounts. You'll own post-sales technical implementation for this segment end to end — from technical discovery and solution design through go-live, adoption, and expansion — working shoulder-to-shoulder with our Customer Activation team, with whom you'll co-own activation milestones and time-to-value.

Strategic customers arrive with multi-entity structures, legacy ERPs, in-flight finance transformations, procurement and treasury requirements, and executive sponsors who expect a named technical leader in the room. Your team is the last line of technical escalation for these accounts — there is no tier above you.

This role suits an experienced leader who can hold two things at once: the operating rigor to run a delivery function at scale, and the technical credibility to sit across from a Controller or VP of Finance and design the solution live.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and grow the Strategic Technical Consulting team — coach senior and principal-level consultants, own hiring, onboarding, performance, and career architecture, and build a bench deep enough to scale with the segment

  • Own post-sales technical implementation for Ramp's largest accounts — accountable for solution quality, delivery timelines, and technical outcomes across the portfolio

  • Co-own activation milestones with Customer Activation — build a joint operating model where TC drives technical design and Activation drives adoption and enablement, with shared accountability for time-to-value and a single, coherent customer experience

  • Serve as the terminal escalation point for complex technical and delivery challenges — ERP integration failures, custom API work, at-risk go-lives, and commitments made pre-sales that need to be re-scoped

  • Define the Strategic delivery model — scoping standards, solution design review, rules of engagement with CSM/AM/Activation, staffing and capacity models, and quality bars that hold up under enterprise scrutiny

  • Run the function with operational rigor — forecast capacity, balance workload across accounts, instrument the team with KPIs (time-to-value, go-live on-time rate, escalation volume, adoption and expansion attach), and use the data in coaching and planning

  • Partner cross-functionally at the leadership level — Customer Activation, Strategic CSM and AM, Sales, Product, Engineering, and GTM Ops — to align on roadmap, feedback loops, and segment strategy

  • Turn field insight into product influence — synthesize what Strategic customers actually need, champion it with Product and Engineering, and close the loop back to the field

  • Set precedent where none exists — make sound calls in ambiguous, high-stakes situations, document the reasoning, and teach the team to do the same

What You Need

  • 8+ years in technical consulting, solutions architecture, implementation, or professional services — with substantial time on enterprise or strategic accounts

  • 3+ years managing individual contributors and owning team-level outcomes; experience managing senior or principal-level ICs strongly preferred

  • Proven track record owning post-sales implementation for large, complex customers — multi-entity, multi-system, executive-sponsored engagements

  • Deep fluency in ERP and financial systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Oracle, Workday Financials, Microsoft Dynamics), APIs, SSO/HRIS integrations, and core accounting workflows (chart of accounts, subsidiaries, approval hierarchies, month-end close)

  • Ability to assess and guide technical solution design at enterprise complexity — and to tell the difference between a configuration problem, a product gap, and a customer process problem

  • Experience building the operating model between two functions — e.g. delivery and onboarding, or services and customer success — and making shared accountability actually work

  • Executive-grade communication — able to hold the room with a CFO or Controller, advocate for your team internally, and translate technical trade-offs into business consequences

  • Demonstrated judgment in ambiguity and a bias toward ownership in a fast-changing, high-growth environment

Nice to Have

  • Experience at an ERP or financial systems vendor (Workday, NetSuite/Oracle, Sage Intacct, Coupa) or in a Big 4 / systems integrator implementation practice

  • Background in fintech, spend management, or AP automation

  • Experience standing up or scaling a technical consulting / professional services function from an early stage

  • Experience managing managers or team leads, or building the career ladder for a technical IC track

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Emerging Talent is an important part of how Ramp builds for the long term. It gives us the opportunity to meet exceptional people early, build relationships before they enter the broader talent market, and develop the next generation of Ramp talent.

We’re hiring a Recruiter to help build and execute our Emerging Talent programs. You’ll own full-cycle recruiting across early-career roles and internships, partnering closely with hiring teams to identify, assess, and close exceptional candidates.

A big part of the job is finding talent before everyone else does. You’ll build relationships with students and early-career candidates, develop new ways to reach high-potential talent, and help create an exceptional experience from a candidate’s first interaction with Ramp through offer and, for our interns, potential conversion to full-time. You’ll also have the opportunity to improve how we operate, test new approaches, and help shape a growing Emerging Talent function.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own full-cycle recruiting across Ramp’s Emerging Talent roles

  • Partner with hiring managers across Engineering, Product, and other teams to define hiring needs, align on candidate profiles, and calibrate on early-career talent

  • Identify and engage high-potential candidates through universities, student communities, technical networks, referrals, events, and other emerging-talent channels

  • Lead offer and closing processes, building strong candidate relationships and helping exceptional talent understand the opportunity to build their careers at Ramp

  • Support the execution of Ramp’s internship programs, including candidate programming, events, intern engagement, and intern-to-full-time conversion

  • Use recruiting data to understand pipeline health, identify opportunities, and keep hiring teams informed on progress and outcomes

  • Create an exceptional candidate experience that is thoughtful, transparent, and high-touch at every stage

  • Experiment with new ways to identify, engage, and hire exceptional talent early, and help turn what works into repeatable recruiting practices

 

What You Need

  • 5+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience; experience with Emerging Talent, university, campus, or early-career recruiting is a plus

  • A track record of identifying and engaging exceptional talent, with strong instincts for candidate quality

  • The ability to quickly learn new talent markets, calibrate to a high hiring bar, and recruit across different roles and functions

  • Strong operational rigor and the ability to manage high-volume pipelines, competing priorities, and frequent context changes without sacrificing candidate quality or experience

  • Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, with the ability to earn trust with candidates, hiring managers, and cross-functional partners

  • An experimental mindset and willingness to try new approaches to find, engage, and hire great talent

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience owning high-volume or seasonal hiring programs

  • Experience recruiting technical or engineering early-career talent

  • Experience supporting internship programs and intern-to-full-time conversion

  • Experience using AI throughout the recruiting workflow to improve sourcing, candidate engagement, and execution

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

About the Role

Ramp is looking for a Performance Marketing Manager to own paid acquisition on YouTube, ChatGPT, X, Rideshare, and Reddit, and to find new incremental channels. You'll take early experiments and turn them into measurable programs and build the operating model that makes successful channels part of Ramp's evergreen performance marketing mix.

This is a high-autonomy role. You will evaluate channel opportunities, design tests, launch campaigns, and analyze full-funnel performance. You'll work with Growth, Creative, Data, Finance, and other cross-functional partners to move quickly while maintaining a high bar for measurement & efficiency.

You’ll use AI as a practical part of the job: building systems that speed up research, campaign creation, performance analysis, and day-to-day channel operations.

What You'll Do

  • Own performance on YouTube, ChatGPT, X, Rideshare, and Reddit. Understand how conversion events, value signals, and lookalike audiences work at a technical level and use that to make channels more efficient over time.

  • Identify, evaluate, and prioritize new performance marketing channels and acquisition opportunities.

  • Build the path from experiment to evergreen program: prove incremental SQLs and pipeline impact, hit LTV-to-CAC efficiency targets, and document a repeatable operating playbook.

  • Own channels as they mature. Decide when a program stays with you and when it transitions to a dedicated owner so you can keep finding new ones.

  • Analyze performance across the full funnel. Turn incomplete or noisy data into a clear call on what to scale, improve, pause, or stop.

  • Partner with data and engineering to improve tracking, attribution, and reporting, and with Creative on messaging, format, and ad concepts across surfaces, audiences, and channels.

  • Build AI agents, workflows, and tools that help the team test more ideas and operationalize channels faster.

What You Need

  • 3+ years in a performance / quantitative marketing, growth, or comparable decision-science role, where you’ve owned numbers and shaped meaningful outcomes.

  • Strong analytical judgment. You can define success metrics, diagnose and isolate performance issues, and make decisions with imperfect information.

  • You enjoy designing experiments and translating results into a clear call on what to fund, scale, or kill.

  • You've built AI workflows, automations, or agents to improve marketing execution and you have good judgment about where AI accelerates the work and where human review is necessary.

  • You move projects from ambiguity to a clear outcome with limited direction and you're detail-oriented in campaign setup, tracking, and measurement.

Nice-to-Haves

  • B2B experience.

  • Experience bringing an experimental channel into a scaled program.

  • Familiarity with attribution, incrementality testing, randomized controlled tests (RCTs), MMM, and marketing measurement.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is seeking its first dedicated Financial Crimes Compliance Controls Senior Strategist to build and own the framework that demonstrates FCC controls are working as intended, remain effective as risk evolves, and can be clearly supported in bank-partner, audit, and regulatory examinations.

This is a senior individual-contributor role at the intersection of financial-crimes compliance, controls effectiveness, technology, data, and AI-enabled operations. You will own FCC’s approach to testing, documenting, and improving manual and automated controls, including procedures, detection rules, AI and LLM-enabled workflows, and automation deployments.

You will serve as FCC’s dedicated compliance partner for program-level Product, Engineering, Design, and Data (“PEDD”) initiatives, ensuring FCC requirements, controls, and risk considerations are incorporated into strategic product and technology planning. This role complements the broader team’s cross-functional partnerships by focusing specifically on major PEDD-led initiatives.

This is a builder role for an experienced financial-crimes compliance professional with deep analytical skills and strong BSA/AML, and sanctions subject-matter expertise You will assess emerging and existing financial-crimes risks, make sound and defensible control decisions, and help build the processes, technology partnerships, and governance needed for FCC to scale responsibly. You will not simply maintain existing processes. You will help shape how FCC’s controls environment, AI strategy, and product partnership model evolve.

What You’ll Do

  • Own FCC’s controls-effectiveness across manual procedures, detection rules, workflow controls, automation deployments, and AI or LLM-enabled capabilities.

  • Establish standards for testing, evidence retention, issue identification, remediation tracking, and ongoing control monitoring.

  • Serve as FCC’s dedicated compliance partner for major PEDD-led initiatives, defining FCC requirements and ensuring compliance needs are incorporated into product and technology planning.

  • Partner with PEDD to translate financial-crimes requirements into scalable workflows, controls, and user experiences.

  • Own FCC’s internal AI and automation strategy, including identifying high-value use cases and ensuring AI-enabled workflows are appropriately tested, documented, monitored, and supported by appropriate human oversight.

  • Use financial crimes domain expertise, data, and analytical methods to proactively evaluate risk coverage, identify emerging risks or control gaps, and drive solutions and improvements..

  • Serve as an independent, qualified secondary reviewer for FCC compliance reviews where segregation of duties or heightened review is required.

What You Need

  • 7+ years of experience in financial-crimes compliance, AML/BSA or sanctions.

  • At least 3 years of experience in a technical compliance, controls, compliance-testing, quality-assurance, or similar role.

  • At least 3 years of experience as an AML or financial-crimes trusted advisor, including partnering with technical, operational, product, or business stakeholders on risk-based controls and decisions.

  • Experience developing, implementing, or evaluating controls across both manual and technology-enabled processes.

  • Deep understanding of financial-crimes typologies and how risk evolves across products, payment flows, customer types, and operational processes.

  • AI fluency, including the ability to independently use approved AI tools, critically assess output quality and limitations, and lead strategic AI and automation initiatives within a compliance environment.

  • Strong data-analysis skills sufficient to assess control performance, evaluate AI or LLM-enabled controls, identify trends or gaps, and partner credibly with technical teams.

  • Experience presenting testing results, control documentation, risk findings, or program materials to regulators, examiners, auditors, or bank partners.

  • ACAMS certification or equivalent financial-crimes certification.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex compliance requirements and risk decisions clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Comfort operating with significant autonomy and building structure in a new, evolving role.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience evaluating or implementing AI, machine learning, LLM, automation, or decisioning controls in a regulated environment.

  • Experience supporting a fintech, payments, banking, card, or money-transmission compliance program.

  • Experience designing controls for transaction monitoring, KYC or KYB, EDD, sanctions screening, suspicious-activity reporting, or payment-risk workflows.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

At Ramp, people are the single biggest lever on our trajectory, and the bar for who joins this team gets higher every quarter, not lower. We are hiring our first dedicated Recruiter for GTM Expansion, based in London: someone who can map a market, identify the operators who will outperform their peers and run a full-cycle process that wins them.

The UK is the immediate mandate. You will partner with local and US-based leaders to turn an ambitious growth plan into a real commercial team, from first conversation through offer close. You will also help us build the recruiting approach, market knowledge and candidate networks that support Ramp's expansion into new GTM markets over time.

The recruiters who do this best combine craft on the front end, research, identification and calibration, with execution on the back end, closing, candidate experience and pipeline discipline. We are looking for both.

What You'll Do

• Own full-cycle recruiting for priority GTM Expansion hiring, starting with UK roles across Sales, Solutions Consulting, Partnerships and Customer Success.

• Build a sharp point of view on the UK market and future expansion markets: the companies producing strong talent, the people who outperform their peers and the communities that matter.

• Use research, data and AI as part of your everyday craft to identify and qualify exceptional candidates. We expect a written market point of view, not just a slate of profiles.

• Run thoughtful, personalised outreach grounded in the candidate's actual background, commercial motion or recent work. We care more about quality, replies and conversion than send volume.

• Partner with GTM leaders to turn ambitious hiring plans into a clear profile, credible process and realistic compensation strategy. Surface hard market truth early and push back constructively when needed.

• Own the candidate experience from first conversation through offer close: fast follow-up, clear communication, strong process discipline and a tailored closing plan for the candidates we most want.

• Build real presence for Ramp in London through the right relationships, referrals and targeted community activity. The point is pipeline and credibility, not events for their own sake.

• Work tightly with the wider GTM Recruiting team on calibration, sourcing support, insight and operating rhythm, while bringing strong local judgment.

• Help improve how Ramp recruits for expansion by capturing what works in the UK and applying it thoughtfully as we enter new markets.

What You Need

• 5+ years of full-cycle GTM or Sales recruiting experience, ideally in a high-growth technology company where quality and pace both mattered.

• Strong knowledge of the UK technology talent market and a credible local network, or clear evidence that you can build one quickly.

• A track record of finding and closing exceptional people, not simply running inherited processes. You can point to candidates you identified who became strong hires.

• Excellent sourcing and research instincts. You can explain why someone is genuinely differentiated, not only that they have the right title at the right company.

• Experience hiring across several GTM functions, such as AEs, Sales Leadership, Solutions Consulting, Partnerships, Customer Success or RevOps.

• Strong candidate-closing judgment. You listen closely, understand what each candidate is weighing and can build conviction against serious alternatives.

• The confidence to influence senior leaders, challenge a mis-scoped search and make a hiring process better without creating unnecessary friction.

• Comfort using data to understand funnel health, diagnose problems and hold an honest conversation about what needs to change.

• High ownership. You book the next step while you have the candidate, chase what is stuck and do not wait for a detailed brief to get useful work moving.

• Specific, sharp written communication. Your outreach and candidate updates should never feel template-driven.

Nice to Have

• Experience recruiting for a fintech, SaaS, infrastructure or similarly complex B2B product.

• Experience joining a company as the first recruiter in a new geography, or helping to scale an international business.

• Experience building an AI-augmented recruiting research workflow.

Why this Role

You will have unusual ownership over one of Ramp's most important growth priorities, with the support of an established Talent team rather than the isolation of a one-person recruiting function. The work is practical and high impact: build the UK commercial team, help leaders make better hiring decisions and raise the bar for how Ramp recruits as it enters new markets.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp Economics Lab is the go-to source for understanding how businesses spend on and adopt AI. Built on Ramp’s $200B+ business spend dataset, our flagship Ramp AI Index tracks the AI economy through actual business spend data. Our research is regularly cited by the Financial Times, The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, The Economist, The New York Times, CNBC, Reuters, Axios, JPMorgan analyst reports, and our favorite independent substacks. You will work with Ara Kharazian, lead economist.

We’re hiring an economics-minded data scientist to own and expand this work: own Ramp AI Index, add new metrics tracking token spend and ROI of AI, extend our research internationally, and publish rigorous but accessible analysis for policymakers, researchers, businesses, the press, and the public.

You’ll also build a new customer-facing economics function from the ground up: developing Ramp’s economic outlook, meeting with customers and prospects, presenting to CFOs and finance teams, and translating our data into practical recommendations for business planning, budgeting, and AI strategy.

This role combines economic judgment, applied data science, public writing, data visualization, and executive communication. You should be able to move from an important question to credible analysis, a clear visual or argument, and advice a business leader can act on.

What You Need

  • Minimum of 5 years of industry experience as a Data Scientist or Economist

  • Strong perspectives on the economics of AI, economic policy, new media, and writing

  • Strong knowledge of SQL (preferably Redshift, Snowflake, BigQuery) and how to write efficient SQL queries

  • Familiarity with BI tools (preferably Looker, Omni, Sigma, Hex or equivalent) and experience distributing data insights via reports and dashboards

  • Track record of shipping high-quality research, writing, and thought leadership under short, non-academic timelines

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, constantly improving, start-up environment that focuses on solving problems with iterative technical solutions

  • Active reader of the news in economics, business, and AI trends

  • An advanced user of AI for data science, and an eye for good charts and web design (we vibecode ramp.com/data ourselves and could use some help)

  • At some point in the recent past, you have been described as “a breath of fresh air.” You will meet with customers and prospects and present data. It’s very important you don’t come off as dry or overly academic

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with the modern data stack (Fivetran / Snowflake / dbt / Looker / Hightouch or equivalents)

  • Experience within the payments and financial technology space

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is building it's UK business from the ground up. We are looking for a Director of Partnerships to be the senior commercial owner of Ramp’s partner ecosystem in the UK: creating the relationships, market presence, and repeatable routes to revenue that help make Ramp a category-defining company in the region.

Reporting to the VP of Channel Sales, you will operate as a founder for Partnerships in London. You will build a focused partner strategy, develop executive-level relationships, and turn the right relationships into durable commercial outcomes. You will work closely with the UK go-to-market team and cross-functional leaders across Sales, Product, Marketing, and Customer Success to make partnerships a meaningful driver of market entry and long-term growth.

This is not a role for someone looking to inherit a mature playbook. The right person is entrepreneurial, commercially sharp, and comfortable creating clarity where there is none. They can move from a first meeting with a senior executive to a clear point of view, an internal plan, and disciplined follow-through.

What You'll Do

  • Own and execute Ramp’s UK partnerships strategy, identifying the partner categories and individual relationships that can accelerate awareness, pipeline, customer value, and long-term market position

  • Build and maintain senior relationships across the UK ecosystem, including accounting, private equity and venture capital firms, professional-services and consulting firms, financial institutions, technology partners, and other high-leverage channels

  • Work alongside the UK Channel Partner Managers, aligning the broader ecosystem strategy with Ramp’s dedicated motions and creating leverage across shared relationships

  • Develop a focused partnership plan for priority relationships: articulate the joint value proposition, define the commercial path, and create mutual accountability for progress

  • Generate measurable commercial impact by sourcing and influencing pipeline, creating warm paths to target customers, and supporting strategic deals through partner relationships

  • Represent Ramp with credibility at executive meetings, industry events, and partner forums, building the company’s reputation as a serious, long-term UK partner

  • Serve as the internal voice of the UK partner market, translating relationship intelligence, customer needs, and market dynamics into actionable input for Sales, Product, Marketing, and leadership

  • Build the operating cadence for the function, including account plans, partnership scorecards, executive briefs, pipeline visibility, and clear follow-through across internal and external stakeholders

  • Help shape Ramp’s broader UK and European go-to-market strategy as the market, team, and partnership portfolio grow

What You Need

  • 10+ years of experience in sales, partnerships, business development, alliances, or go-to-market leadership, with a demonstrated record of building senior relationships and driving commercial outcomes

  • A proven track record of owning revenue, quota, influenced pipeline, or similarly concrete commercial goals in a complex B2B environment

  • Executive presence and sound judgment: you can earn credibility with senior partner leaders and represent Ramp confidently in consequential conversations

  • A builder mindset. You have launched a territory, vertical, business line, or partner motion, and know how to create a plan and operating rhythm from a blank page

  • The ability to turn broad relationships into specific opportunities, navigate multiple stakeholders, and maintain momentum through long sales and partnership cycles

  • Strong strategic and analytical thinking, with the ability to decide where Ramp should invest and make a clear, data-informed case to senior leadership

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to build a compelling partnership narrative and align cross-functional teams around it

  • AI fluency as a daily habit. Ramp is a builder culture: if you do not instinctively reach for AI before doing things manually, this role will be a hard adjustment

  • Ability to work five days per week from Ramp’s London office, with willingness to travel across the UK and continental Europe as needed

Nice to Haves

  • Experience selling or partnering into private equity, financial services, consulting, enterprise technology, or high-growth software companies

  • Experience in fintech, financial software, payments, spend management, or the office of the CFO technology ecosystem

  • An established UK network of senior commercial, investment, operating, or technology leaders

  • Experience building a new market or international go-to-market motion

  • Fluency in an additional European language

Why Ramp

  • Own one of Ramp’s most important external-facing growth mandates as we build the UK business

  • Work directly with senior leaders across Channel, Sales, Product, and Marketing, with the autonomy to shape the market strategy and the accountability to deliver commercial outcomes

  • Build at the intersection of fintech, AI, and enterprise software at a company redefining how businesses manage spend

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp builds software that moves real money, from bill payments and corporate cards to reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running: invoices get paid, books get closed, and finance leaders can trust the data behind every decision.

In this role, you will be the person who spots where customers are getting stuck and drives issues to a clear resolution. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. This is not script-based support. You will triage, investigate, and make high-signal judgment calls throughout the day.

You will thrive in this role if you are a systems thinker and deeply customer obsessed. Support is the baseline. How you think about improving processes, tools, and outcomes is what sets you apart.

What You’ll Do

  • Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat.

  • Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break.

  • Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows.

  • Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp.

  • Ship improvements, not just flag them. When you notice a process gap, a missing SOP, or a knowledge base article that's sending associates down the wrong path, you don't just raise it — you have the autonomy to roll up your sleeves and fix it. Leverage AI to solve problems, build automations, and improve the systems around you. The best people in this role make the whole team better.

  • Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler.

What You Need

  • You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again.

  • You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement.

  • You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction.

  • You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code.

  • You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through.

  • You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon.

  • You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there.

  • You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting

  • Familiarity with accounting workflows (AP/AR, GL, reconciliation) or ERP integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage)

  • Background in payments infrastructure (ACH, wire transfers, card networks)

  • Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up

Why be a CX Associate at Ramp

  • Cross-functional exposure from day one. You work directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams — not siloed into a support queue.

  • AI tools and unlimited access. Unlimited tokens, proprietary AI tools like Glass, and a culture that expects you to use them to move faster and build smarter.

  • Career growth that you own. Grow within CX, explore other functions internally, or carve out a path that doesn't exist yet. If you're invested, we're invested.

  • Culture that's different from a call center. Team events, in-person offsites, and a genuine commitment to building a team people want to be part of.

Read more about how Ramp thinks about AI and CX:

  • How Ramp Became an AI-First Company — Geoff Charles, CPO

  • Inside Glass: How Ramp Built a Proprietary AI Platform for CX — Seb Goddijn, AI Product Manager

  • AI-Powered Customer Experience at Ramp — Ben Levick, Head of CX / Ramp AI

What to know before you apply

  • Schedule & Shift Bidding - Please Read Carefully: CX Associates work a set 40-hour/week schedule assigned through a schedule-bid process. Working hours span 7:00 AM–11:00 PM local time (EST/ CST/ PST), and your shift will likely include a weekend day (either Sun–Thu or Tue–Sat). Associates also cover 2–3 company holidays per year on a rotating basis. Ramp's customers operate on financial deadlines that don't pause.

  • The product changes frequently. If you need a stable, predictable environment, this isn't it. If you like learning new things every week, it is.

  • This role is a launchpad for your career at one of the fastest-growing companies in fintech.

For candidates located in NYC or SF, the pay range for this role is $60,000-$70,000. For candidates located in all other locations, the pay range for this role is $60,000-$65,000.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is hiring Executive Assistants to partner with senior leaders across the company. Our EAs play a critical role in helping executives operate at their best—creating focus, removing friction, anticipating needs, and ensuring important work moves forward.

This is more than calendar and logistics management. You’ll serve as a trusted partner to your executives, using strong judgment, operational rigor, and modern tools to create leverage in a fast-moving environment. The work is highly visible and constantly evolving, offering exposure to some of Ramp’s most important teams, priorities, and decisions.

We are currently hiring two Executive Assistants to support leaders across Finance and Legal. We generally look for the same core qualities across our EA team: exceptional judgment, discretion, adaptability, and the ability to build trusted partnerships. During the initial conversations, we’ll learn more about your experience and preferences and discuss where there may be the strongest mutual fit.

This role is based in our New York City office. We default to being in the office at least three days a week.

What You'll Do

  • Partner closely with senior leaders to manage their time, priorities, and day-to-day execution

  • Own complex, high-volume calendar management across multiple executives, navigating frequent changes and competing priorities

  • Manage executive inboxes as needed, including triaging communications, drafting responses, flagging urgent matters, and ensuring important items receive timely attention

  • Coordinate domestic and international travel with close attention to efficiency, executive preferences, and changing business needs

  • Plan and execute leadership meetings, offsites, team events, customer or partner engagements, and cross-functional working sessions

  • Draft, organize, and manage communications on behalf of executives when appropriate

  • Serve as a central coordination point across internal teams and external stakeholders, ensuring clarity, alignment, and follow-through

  • Track action items, deadlines, and commitments, proactively prompting executives and partners to keep work moving

  • Manage budgets, expenses, and vendor relationships on behalf of executives

  • Handle sensitive business, financial, legal, customer, and personnel information with exceptional discretion

  • Identify inefficiencies and build lightweight systems, documentation, and workflows that improve speed and organization

  • Use AI, automation, and modern tooling to eliminate repetitive work and create greater leverage for yourself and your executives

  • Continuously look for ways to anticipate needs and improve how work gets done

What You Need

  • 3+ years of experience supporting senior executives in a fast-paced, high-accountability environment

  • Proven ability to manage complex calendars, shifting priorities, and multiple high-priority workstreams

  • Strong organizational instincts and exceptional attention to detail—you anticipate what’s needed and ensure nothing falls through the cracks

  • Sound judgment about when to act independently, when to seek context, and when to escalate

  • High discretion and comfort handling sensitive or confidential information

  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication skills

  • High EQ and the ability to build trust quickly with executives, cross-functional partners, and external stakeholders

  • A proactive, ownership-oriented approach—you identify what needs to happen and move it forward without waiting to be asked

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and adapting as priorities evolve

  • Strong proficiency with Google Workspace, Slack, and other modern collaboration tools

  • Demonstrated use of AI, automation, or tooling to streamline work and reduce manual effort

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience supporting multiple executives simultaneously

  • Experience supporting leaders in GTM, Finance, Legal, or another externally facing or highly confidential function

  • Background in a high-growth or scaling company

  • Experience coordinating with customers, investors, partners, advisors, or external counsel

  • Experience managing executive inboxes and drafting communications

  • Track record of building systems or processes that improve team speed and execution

  • Fluency with workflow automation, bots, or AI assistants

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

What You’ll Do

  • Build account strategies using company context, growth signals, financial workflows, and stakeholder priorities.

  • Research and engage finance leaders through personalized phone, email, and multi-channel outreach.

  • Qualify prospects through consultative discovery, connecting workflow challenges to business impact.

  • Clearly explain how Ramp can help finance teams simplify spend management, reduce manual work, and gain visibility and control across financial operations.

  • Handle objections with sound judgment and earn the right to a next conversation.

  • Partner with Account Executives on account planning, sequencing, and opportunity creation.

  • Use AI and other tools thoughtfully to strengthen research, prioritization, personalization, and workflow efficiency; validate outputs before using them.

  • Maintain accurate prospect and activity data in Salesforce and use performance data to improve outreach quality.

What You’ll Need

  • Proven SDR/BDR, closing, or equivalent quota-carrying experience, with measurable evidence of attainment or overachievement.

  • If transitioning from a non-sales background, a demonstrated record of exceptional performance in that field, supported by specific outcomes.

  • Experience prioritizing accounts, engaging senior or complex buyers, and tailoring outreach to customer context.

  • Strong written and verbal communication: concise, customer-focused, and specific.

  • Strong discovery and objection-handling fundamentals.

  • Commercial judgment: form a point of view, explain tradeoffs, and adapt based on new information.

  • A builder mindset: identify improvements, create repeatable systems, and learn from results.

  • Practical AI fluency and sound judgment using tools to improve quality and speed.

  • A data-driven approach to performance: diagnose results, seek feedback, and change behavior.

  • Interest in building a long-term sales career and taking on the scope of a Mid-Market SDR role.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience selling into finance, accounting, operations, or technology teams.

  • Experience in B2B SaaS, fintech, or another high-growth environment.

  • Familiarity with Salesforce, sales engagement platforms, intent data, or account research tools.

  • Experience collaborating with Account Executives on account-based or multi-stakeholder selling.

  • Familiarity with finance workflows, expense management, accounts payable, procurement, or Enterprise Resource Planning Systems (ERPs) is a strong plus.

  • Prior CPA or Audit experience is a strong plus.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp’s Sales organization is looking for self-motivated teammates who are excited to learn the craft of outbound selling and help accelerate our growth. As an SMB Sales Development Representative, you will be an early point of contact for prospective customers by researching, engaging, and qualifying finance leaders at growing businesses.

This is a foundational sales role for early-career talent. You will build prospecting, discovery, messaging, and account-prioritization skills through structured training, coaching, feedback, and repetition.

What You’ll Do

  • Source new sales opportunities through inbound qualification and outbound outreach.

  • Research companies, prioritize accounts, and identify the right prospects to contact.

  • Build thoughtful phone, email, and multi-channel campaigns that create relevant conversations with finance leaders.

  • Qualify prospects through consultative discovery and uncover business challenges before positioning Ramp.

  • Clearly explain how Ramp can help finance teams simplify spend management, reduce manual work, and gain visibility and control.

  • Maintain accurate prospect and activity data in Salesforce and other sales tools.

  • Use AI and other tools thoughtfully to improve research, personalization, and workflow efficiency; validate outputs before using them.

  • Use coaching, data, and feedback to improve performance and contribute qualified pipeline.

What You’ll Need

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and concisely.

  • Curiosity about business challenges and how finance teams operate.

  • Comfort in a fast-paced, high-volume environment that includes repetition, feedback, and rejection.

  • A builder mindset: you spot friction, create simple improvements, learn from results, and adapt quickly.

  • Demonstrated coachability and willingness to ask for help, practice, and improve.

  • Practical AI fluency and sound judgment when using tools to improve work quality and speed.

  • A genuine interest in beginning a sales career and building foundational outbound skills.

Nice to Haves

  • Customer-facing, sales, fundraising, service, or leadership experience.

  • Experience working toward goals, metrics, or performance targets.

  • Familiarity with CRM, outreach, or productivity tools.

  • Exposure to a high-growth or ambiguous environment.

  • Interest in finance operations, spend management, or B2B technology.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

You will build and run the operating systems that help Juno ship reliably and support customers as we scale. On the product operations side, you will turn product decisions into clear operating plans, maintain visibility in Linear, coordinate customer testing and launch readiness, keep commitments and risks visible, and make sure product changes are communicated clearly.

You will partner closely with product and engineering to make decisions executable, keep work organized, surface gaps and dependencies, and ensure the team follows through on what it has committed to ship.

On the customer support side, you will be the first line of defense when customers encounter product issues. You will triage and investigate problems, coordinate the right response, and redirect travel-service questions to our travel partners. Because you sit close to both the product process and the customer, you will turn recurring friction into clear insights, accountable follow-up, and better operating systems.

Success means Juno ships through a lightweight and dependable process, customers understand what changed, risks and commitments do not get lost, recurring issues reach the right owners, and support demand does not grow one-for-one with the business.

What You’ll Do

  • Provide holistic support through the entire launch lifecycle across program management, customer testing, launch readiness, change management, customer communication, and post-launch iteration. Own and improve Juno's shipping process so the right reviews, testing, documentation, internal enablement, and customer updates happen at the right time.

  • Maintain Linear as a reliable operating system for projects, owners, milestones, dependencies, status, and product decisions. Surface risks early and follow through until they are resolved.

  • Serve as the first line of defense for product-related customer issues across email and chat, join customer calls when needed, manage escalations to resolution, and route travel-service questions to the right partner.

  • Be the voice of the customer in product decisions. Analyze support trends and customer feedback, diagnose recurring friction, size the problems you find, and translate messy input into clear findings, recommended actions, prioritization input, and accountable follow-up for product and engineering.

  • Build AI-powered workflows, automations, knowledge systems, and self-service experiences that improve the quality and speed of product operations and customer support.

What You Need

  • 3+ years of experience in product operations, program management, customer experience, technical support, consulting, or another customer-facing analytical role in a fast-moving software company.
