About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

The Ramp Travel team builds the travel booking and management platform built-in to Ramp. We build the capabilities that allows travelers to stay productive on the road: flight and hotel search, booking and checkout, our agentic travel assistant, and on-the-go mobile trip guidance. We also own the capabilities that ensure companies are spending their travel dollars effectively: travel policy evaluation, supplier and TMC integrations and benchmarking, and data insights.

Growing the sophistication and global reach of the Travel product is a top strategic priority at Ramp. The work this team does directly enables Ramp to to support some of the largest and most interesting customers in the world.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead, mentor, coach, and grow the Ramp Travel engineering team (~6 engineers today).

  • Own delivery across our travel management surfaces: search and inventory, quoting and repricing, checkout, policy evaluation, loyalty, post-booking servicing.

  • Own reliability and correctness of a system dependent on third parties: supplier APIs, GDS and aggregator content, TMC and OBT integrations.

  • Partner with Product, Design, Ops, Partnerships, and Sales on enterprise travel commitments.

  • Set the team's practices for AI-assisted development and ship agentic booking features.

  • Hire. The team is expected to grow.

What You'll Need

  • 2+ years managing engineers, team size roughly 5 to 15.

  • High levels of ownership. Comfortability taking difficult ambiguous problems and driving successful execution.

  • Has built something 0→1 and then scaled it.

  • Willing to be hands-on. This is a six-person team, and everyone at Ramp is a builder.

  • Current enough technically to lead a design review and evaluate an architecture proposal.

  • Strong product judgment and comfort talking to customers.

  • Has owned a transactional system with external dependencies: booking, payments, marketplace, or logistics.

Preferred

  • Corporate travel domain experience, such as: corporate online booking tools (OBTs), integrations with travel content sources (GDS/NDC), and front-end traveler experiences.

  • Enterprise B2B fintech or T&E background.

  • Has rolled out agentic dev tooling to a team, or shipped LLM-backed features.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

About the Role

Emerging Talent is an important part of how Ramp builds for the long term. It gives us the opportunity to meet exceptional people early, build relationships before they enter the broader talent market, and develop the next generation of Ramp talent.

We’re hiring an Emerging Talent Operations Associate to help run the operational foundation behind our internship and new-grad programs. You’ll partner with recruiters, coordinators, hiring managers, People Ops, and IT to keep candidate data, interviews, offers, onboarding, and intern support moving smoothly.

You’ll help create an exceptional experience from a candidate’s first interaction with Ramp through offer and, for interns, potential conversion to full-time. This is a hands-on role for someone organized and resourceful who enjoys making complex programs feel seamless. As you learn the work, you’ll help improve processes, templates, and simple automations.

This is a temporary, full-time role with strong potential to convert to a permanent full-time position.

What You'll Do

  • Support daily operations across the internship and new-grad recruiting lifecycle.

  • Maintain accurate candidate, event, and program data in Ashby.

  • Partner with recruiting coordinators on candidate communications during high-volume periods.

  • Support job and offer administration, including requisitions, approvals, and documentation.

  • Help coordinate onboarding, access, housing, and other intern and new-hire needs.

  • Track recurring work, flag risks early, and keep important details from slipping.

  • Improve team templates, checklists, and operating processes.

  • Identify repetitive work that could be simplified with AI or practical automation.

  • During slower operational periods, support program management.

What You Need

  • 1–3 years of experience in recruiting coordination, talent or program operations, university recruiting, events, or another detail-heavy service role. Equivalent experience is welcome.

  • Strong organization, follow-through, and attention to detail.

  • Clear, warm communication, timely updates, and reliable follow-through.

  • Comfort managing shifting priorities in a fast-moving environment.

  • Curiosity about learning new tools and improving how work gets done.

  • Good judgment, ownership, and a habit of raising issues early.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Ashby, Greenhouse, or another applicant-tracking system.

  • Familiarity working with Talent, People Ops, IT, Workplace, or Payroll.

  • Experience improving a process, tracker, template, or workflow.

Don’t check every box? We’d still love to hear from you. Care, curiosity, and strong follow-through matter most.

About the Role

As a Product Operations partner for Ramp Procurement, you will help build and scale the workflows that enable customers to manage their procurement processes with speed, accuracy, and control. You will improve both the requester and approver experience while shaping product quality through data, customer feedback, and tight partnership with customer-facing internal teams.

Beyond your product vertical, you will also contribute to Product Operations process improvement and product building that allows our Product and Engineering teams to scale. You will use AI tools to improve release management, collect customer feedback, and enable internal teams to support customers and troubleshoot issues.

Our main goal is to reduce customer friction, measured by support tickets per active user and customer NPS.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the voice-of-customer loop for Procurement — systematically capture, analyze, and prioritize feedback from CX, Sales, and direct customer channels

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, and Design to translate customer feedback into actionable product requirements and specs

  • Own launch operations for new Procurement features as they move from Alpha to GA, including AI-native experiences that require strong customer and internal enablement

  • Directly ship product improvements (UX fixes and paper cuts) using AI tools — owning your own backlog of customer friction reduction, not just feeding the engineering backlog

  • Use AI to automate processes and build products that enable teams to ship faster while maintaining a high quality bar

  • Build scalable operating systems for release readiness, internal enablement, supportability, and issue escalation across Procurement workflows

What You Need

  • 3+ years in product operations, product management, or a customer-facing analytical role supporting B2B SaaS; experience with procurement, intake and approval workflows, spend management, or financial operations preferred

  • Proficiency using data to size opportunities and analyze adoption, support trends, payment flow performance, and customer friction

  • Ability to translate qualitative feedback into crisp requirements and operational processes

  • Comfort working in ambiguous, technically complex spaces and driving clarity across multiple stakeholders

  • Strong problem solving, prioritization, and communication skills; bias to ship improvements quickly and measure impact

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Principal Brand Designer to define the brand design system that takes Ramp into new futures. You’ll turn our strategy into design, lead our most important brand projects, and help the team do its best work.

This is a leadership individual contributor role. You can take any idea from zero to one. You understand the business fundamentals, the product value, the channels that perform best, and you know where brand design amplifies and improves the work. You understand each XFN’s accountability and outcomes, from product, marketing, GTM, growth and beyond. You can speak their language.

What You'll Do

  • Set creative direction. Turn business goals and audience insights into clear ideas for the brand.

  • Lead company-defining projects. Take campaigns, launches, and other brand experiences from an open question to finished work.

  • Set the bar for quality and taste. You are the go-to expert for typography, imagery, layout, and brand design. You are the champion for this standard.

  • Build the brand system. Evolve our visual identity over time. We believe in coherency over consistency. We built our brand system to behave like jazz.

  • Connect brand and product. Work with product, marketing, and engineering so the company feels coherent wherever people experience it.

  • Raise the quality of the team’s work. You are a player-coach that can mentor others and develop a culture of collaboration, creativity, and trust.

  • Tell stories to drive alignment. Help partners understand the thinking, agree on a direction, and make practical choices about scope and timing.

What makes you stand out

  • You’re already using AI tooling and agents to explore faster, iterate sooner, and develop ideas that you couldn’t before.

  • You have both agency and in-house experience.

  • You have side hobbies exploring design and creativity. We want to see side projects that show a desire for learning, a student-like mindset, and above all, enthusiasm for where the future is headed.

  • You’re humble, thoughtful, and self-aware.

  • Your portfolio reveals a story about how you’ve grown as a person, your interests, and curiosities.

  • You understand that execution is how good ideas win.

What you’ll bring

  • A deep portfolio of brand identities, marketing campaigns, bringing brand into product experiences, and digital applications, with a clear explanation of your contribution.

  • Excellent design fundamentals and the ability to carry an idea through to finished work.

  • Experience leading complex projects independently and making good decisions when the brief is still taking shape.

  • The ability to negotiate, compromise, or understand trade-offs with executives and XFN partners.

  • The ability to connect creative choices to the audience, the product, and the business.

  • A record of helping other designers improve and working well with people across disciplines.

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Ramp is in a critical phase of growth, and paid social is one of the fastest ways we reach new businesses. This role owns the day-to-day of Meta, LinkedIn, and TikTok ads: building campaigns, getting them live, and tuning them once they’re running.   • Help operate our paid Meta, LinkedIn, and TikTok programs, including hands-on campaign setup, targeting, budgets, tracking, QA, reporting, and daily optimization.

  • Translate performance data into clear recommendations for creative, targeting, and testing.

  • Own smaller campaigns and product launches end to end, from stakeholder alignment and briefing through build, deployment post-launch analysis, and reporting.

  • Partner with creative strategists, designers, copywriters, product marketers, and analytics teams to bring campaigns to market.

  • Develop structured testing plans across audiences, creative, messaging, formats, and placements

  • Maintain strong operational standards across naming conventions, documentation, measurement, and campaign governance.

  • Identify opportunities to improve workflows through templates, automation, and AI-enabled tools.

  • Grow into channel planning and broader paid acquisition strategy.

  • 4+ years of experience managing paid social or performance marketing campaigns

  • Deep hands-on experience with Meta Ads Manager and LinkedIn Campaign Manager

  • A strong understanding of campaign structure, audience targeting, bidding, budgeting, tracking, attribution, and optimization

  • Experience working across both creative testing and media execution

  • Experience building repeatable campaign templates, operating systems, and AI-assisted workflows

  • Ability to interpret performance data and turn it into clear, actionable decisions

  • Strong project management skills and confidence owning initiatives from brief through launch

  • Excellent attention to detail, particularly when building, trafficking, and QAing campaigns

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced, test-and-learn environment

  • Strong cross-functional communication and stakeholder-management skills

  • A proactive, ownership-oriented approach and an interest in growing into broader strategic responsibility

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience in paid social for B2B, SaaS, fintech, or financial products

  • Experience leading integrated product or feature launches

  • Knowledge of incrementality testing, experimentation frameworks, and measurement strategy

  • Experience with landing-page testing and conversion-rate optimization

  • Familiarity with marketing analytics, automation, and reporting tools

  • A strong point of view on what makes paid creative effective across different platforms

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is redefining how businesses manage their finances, and our growth marketing team is how millions of businesses first hear that story. As we expand internationally, paid ads are one of our highest-leverage channels — and localized, high-craft creative is what makes them work in a new market.

Based in our London office, you'll own the creative that powers Ramp's international acquisition engine across Meta, LinkedIn, Reddit, and Direct Mail. You'll take the playbook we've built in the US and adapt it for the UK and EU — shaping how Ramp shows up across paid social, video, and display for international audiences. You'll work closely with our Performance Marketing team to turn ideas into ads that move metrics, while pushing the creative bar on what a finance brand can look and feel like abroad.

This is a temporary full-time role, based in London.

What You'll Do

  • Design and animate paid creative end-to-end across static and motion formats, tailored for international markets.

  • Create and localize ads for Meta, LinkedIn, Reddit, and emerging channels across the UK and EU.

  • Adapt the US growth creative playbook for international audiences — and flag where local nuance means it needs to break, not just translate.

  • Develop scalable design and motion systems that help the team move faster while maintaining a high creative bar.

  • Concept hooks, headlines, visual treatments, and creative variants that earn attention and drive performance in-market.

  • Partner closely with Performance Marketing, copywriters, and product marketers (largely US-based) to bring ideas to life across time zones.

  • Iterate quickly based on performance data and contribute to international testing strategy.

  • Build templates, automations, AI workflows, and creative systems that increase team velocity.

  • Explore new tools, techniques, and AI-native workflows to expand what's possible inside our production pipeline.

  • Help evolve how Ramp's brand shows up across international growth marketing.

What You Need

  • 5+ years of experience in visual design, motion design, or creative production

  • Strong portfolio demonstrating both static and motion work

  • Experience creating performance-driven creative for paid acquisition channels

  • Strong taste and a clear point of view on what makes great advertising — with an eye for what resonates in UK/EU markets

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, test-and-learn environment where speed and iteration matter

  • Ability to use performance data and business outcomes as creative feedback

  • Comfort collaborating with a primarily US-based team across time zones

  • Expertise in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite (particularly After Effects)

  • Based in or able to work from the London office

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience building automations, templates, component systems, scripts, or internal creative tooling

  • Fluency with AI tools such as Runway, Veo, Kling, Midjourney, ElevenLabs, Claude Code, or similar

  • Experience creating short-form video for Reels, Shorts, TikTok, and paid social

  • Experience creating or localizing creative for multiple international markets

  • Experience in finance, fintech, SaaS, or other high-growth technology companies

  • Familiarity with performance marketing and growth experimentation frameworks

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior Corporate Paralegal to join Ramp's Legal team and own the operational backbone of how we govern and structure the company. Ramp runs a growing portfolio of U.S. and non-U.S. entities — including regulated and licensed subsidiaries — across a business that ships constantly and raises, acquires, and expands on short notice. You will be the person who keeps that machinery accurate, current, and audit-ready.

This is a broad generalist role. You'll sit at the center of corporate governance, entity management, equity administration, and litigation/employment and you'll partner directly with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Treasury, Compliance, Equity Admin, and People, and outside counsel. We are a small, high-leverage team supporting a company that moves quickly, so you'll cover a lot of ground and be trusted to run matters independently.

What You'll Do

  • Corporate governance: Prepare board and stockholder meeting materials, agendas, minutes, written consents, resolutions, secretary's certificates, and incumbency certificates. Track and calendar governance obligations across the entity portfolio.

  • Entity management: Own the full lifecycle of entity administration — formations and dissolutions, foreign qualifications, annual reports, franchise tax filings, registered agent management, signatories, officer and director lists, post-integration cleanup.

  • KYC, UBO, and diligence: Respond to KYC/UBO and diligence requests from bank partners, regulators, auditors, insurers, and counterparties, and build reusable packages.

  • Equity support: Support equity administration, option and RSU grants, board approvals of equity awards, secondaries, and equity plan recordkeeping in partnership with Finance and People.

  • Transaction support: Run diligence support, signature collection, closing checklists, closing binders, and post-closing obligations for financings, credit facilities, M&A, real estate, and insurance renewals.

  • Commercial and cross-functional support: Assist with powers of attorney, delegations of authority, and corporate approvals needed by the business.

  • Employment support: Support employment- and immigration-related requests and filings.

  • Litigation support: Support subpoena and law enforcement requests, legal holds, e-discovery, and document production. Review and respond to garnishment orders and UCC liens. Serve as Ramp’s custodian of records and as Ramp’s representative in small claims court cases.

What You Need

  • 6+ years of corporate paralegal experience at a major law firm and/or in-house at a high-growth technology or financial services company.

  • Deep working knowledge of corporate governance, entity formation and maintenance, corporate recordkeeping, and secretary's office functions.

  • Excellent drafting skills across resolutions, consents, certificates, and corporate documentation, with genuine precision — you catch the wrong entity name, the stale date, and the missing signature block.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently run multiple time-sensitive workstreams without dropping threads or waiting to be asked.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the judgment to work directly with executives, board members, outside counsel, and cross-functional partners.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift and processes are still being built — and a bias toward action.

  • High judgment around confidential and sensitive corporate information.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to Have

  • Experience at a fintech, payments, or regulated financial services company, including support for licensed entities (money transmitter, EMI, or similar).

  • Experience supporting venture financings, secondaries, M&A integration, or IPO readiness.

  • International entity management experience across EMEA, APAC, LATAM, or Canada.

  • Experience with equity administration and cap table platforms (e.g., Shareworks).

  • Experiencing with litigation or employment matters.

  • Notary Public commission (NY or CA), or willingness to obtain one.

  • ABA-approved paralegal certificate.

  • A track record of using AI or automation to eliminate manual legal work.

About the Role

Ramp is, at its core, an engineering company. We’re looking for backend engineering interns (12 or 16-week co-ops) excited to solve challenging technical problems and ship products used by real customers.

You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and own meaningful projects from inception to production. We value strong technical fundamentals, high ownership, and people who learn quickly, whether or not they’re familiar with our stack.

What You’ll Do

  • Build performant, reliable, and scalable systems powering Ramp’s products

  • Own meaningful projects from design through launch

  • Solve problems across areas like payments, risk and fraud, financial infrastructure, data, and AI

  • Work closely with product and business teams to understand customer needs and improve our products

  • Contribute to engineering tools and systems that help Ramp scale

What You’ll Need

  • Currently pursuing a B.S. or higher in Computer Science or a related technical field, graduating December 2027 or later

  • Strong computer science and programming fundamentals

  • Track record of building and shipping high-quality products, features, or projects

  • Ability to turn ambiguous product and business problems into engineering solutions

  • Desire to learn quickly, take ownership, and work in a fast-paced environment

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with or interest in Python and backend development

  • Familiarity with or desire to learn our stack, including Flask, PostgreSQL, Temporal, Elixir, and AWS

  • Interest in fintech, AI, or building products at scale

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Explore our Engineering Blog & Emerging Talent Blog to learn more about how we build at Ramp and what it’s like to start your career here.

About the Role

Ramp is, at its core, an engineering company, and is on a mission to build the best engineering team in the US! We are looking for iOS interns (12 or 16 weeks) who are excited to be part of our story and help us build a diverse and vibrant tech community. We hire engineers with a broad set of technical skills, who are highly cross-functional, and eager to solve a wide range of engineering challenges. Our ideal candidate has a strong sense of ownership and enjoys owning projects from inception to scaling them in production. We value people who take pride in their work, and show an aptitude for learning quickly whether they’re familiar with our stack or not. You'll be working with a nimble team of committed and talented engineers and having a large, long-term impact on technical design and engineering culture.

What You’ll Do

  • Build and ship new features for Ramp’s iOS app

  • Work alongside experienced engineers and contribute to our mobile codebase

  • Collaborate with Product and Design to bring new features and experiences to life

  • Learn from customer feedback and help continuously improve our product

  • Contribute to engineering tools and processes that help the team move quickly and scale

What You’ll Need

  • Currently pursuing a B.S. or higher in Computer Science or a related technical field, graduating December 2027 or later

  • Experience with Swift and/or iOS development through internships, coursework, or personal projects

  • Strong programming fundamentals and understanding of mobile development concepts

  • Experience building a mobile app, feature, or relevant project

  • Ability to turn product ideas into thoughtful engineering solutions

  • Desire to learn quickly, take ownership, and work in a fast-paced environment

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with SwiftUI

  • Familiarity with mobile design patterns and best practices

  • Experience shipping an iOS app or feature to real users

  • Exposure to technologies in our mobile stack, including Swift Concurrency, The Composable Architecture, Bazel, OpenAPI, or Buildkite

  • Experience with web or backend development

Compensation

  • The monthly rate for this internship is $12,500 USD + housing stipend

Ramp Benefits

  • Apple MacBook

  • Catered Lunches in NYC office Monday-Friday

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

How we build software is changing. Designers are building tools and agents, prototyping in code, and shipping directly into the product. More people can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less.

We’re looking for a Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into the foundations of Ramp.

This is not just about maintaining a component library. It’s about making it possible for designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Ramp—without a designer driving every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change.

You’re a designer first, with the technical depth to guide architecture and get into the code. You have exceptional taste and strong opinions about typography, hierarchy, interaction, and motion. Just as importantly, you know how to turn that judgment into patterns, tools, and guidance that make everyone else’s work better.

You’re deeply curious about AI and already using it to change how you work. You build, experiment, inspect the results, and push past the demo. You can imagine a different way of building software—and lead a team toward it.

This role is for you if you’re excited by:

  • Making great design reproducible. Raise the quality of Ramp’s product and encode what makes it good, so people and agents can produce coherent, usable experiences by default. The system should make excellent work easier, not make every experience look the same.

  • Reimagining what a design system can be. Build beyond components and tokens into composition, interaction patterns, agent guidance, and evaluations. Connect exploration and production so the fastest way to build is also a path to great quality.

  • Leading a team that multiplies everyone else’s impact. Create clear direction, ambitious goals, and a caring yet demanding environment. Inspire curiosity, develop people, and stay close enough to the work to help make it exceptional.

The opportunity is to raise the floor for everyone building at Ramp, while giving designers more room to make the most important experiences extraordinary.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and develop the design systems team. Set clear priorities, ownership, and goals. Give direct, timely feedback, hold people accountable, and help them do the best work of their careers.

  • Own the system’s vision and direction. Decide what to preserve, evolve, simplify, or replace based on what builders and customers need. Turn that direction into focused work the team can deliver.

  • Elevate Ramp’s visual and interaction design. Raise the bar for typography, hierarchy, density, motion, responsive behavior, accessibility, and the states beyond the happy path.

  • Make design judgment usable by people and agents. Translate principles into reusable patterns, reference experiences, composition rules, and guidance that produce better work without you in the room.

  • Guide technical architecture with engineering. Shape everything from components and tokens to how agents discover guidance, compose interfaces, and check their work. Make sound tradeoffs between flexibility, coherence, performance, and ease of use.

  • Stay hands-on. Build prototypes, work in code, and get into implementation details to test ideas, unblock the team, and understand where the system breaks down.

  • Define and measure quality. Build repeatable evaluations grounded in real tasks. Measure whether builders can ship better work faster, with less rework—not just whether they use the tools.

  • Improve the path from idea to shipped experience. Partner with engineering and AI teams on workflows that support fast exploration, useful iteration, and appropriate production safeguards.

  • Earn adoption. Work alongside product teams, listen closely, teach through examples, and turn recurring questions and exceptions into improvements to the system.

  • Keep the team moving forward. Experiment as models and tools evolve, share what you learn, and change direction when the evidence calls for it.

What You Need

  • Experience leading and developing strong design or design engineering teams, with a track record of setting direction and delivering meaningful outcomes.

  • Exceptional visual and interaction design skills. Your work shows a clear point of view, attention to detail, and an ability to make complex experiences feel simple.

  • Deep systems thinking and experience building systems that other teams actually adopt. You can show how your work improved both their speed and the quality of what shipped.

  • Strong technical fluency. You can prototype and build in code, understand front-end architecture, and work through implementation tradeoffs with engineers—not just hand off specifications.

  • Active, hands-on use of AI in your design and building workflow. You understand where it helps, where it fails, and how to improve its output rather than accept it.

  • Experience turning design principles into practical guidance, reusable patterns, and quality checks that work at scale.

  • Strong product judgment and a habit of staying close to the people using what you build. You connect system decisions to real workflows and customer outcomes.

  • The ability to create clarity in ambiguity, make decisions, give difficult feedback, and maintain momentum without losing the quality bar.

  • Curiosity that borders on obsession about how AI changes software and how we build it—and the ability to ignite that curiosity in others.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience building agent-usable design guidance, generation workflows, or evaluations for design quality.

  • Experience building developer or designer tools that became part of other teams’ daily workflow.

  • Experience leading a major design-system migration or company-wide change in how teams build.

  • Experience evolving a system across platforms or connecting product and brand experiences.

  • Founder or early-stage startup experience.

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About Production Engineering

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

  • One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

  • If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

  • We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

  • We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

  • We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

 

Our Teams

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across four areas:

  • Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale

  • Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

  • Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture

  • Internal Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs

 

What You'll Do

Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure. You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team.

Day to day, you will:

  • Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale.

  • Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved.

  • Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time.

  • Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs.

  • Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers.

  • Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE.

  • Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom.

  • Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done.

 

What We Look For

We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team.

The mindset we're looking for:

  • You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem.

  • You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job.

  • You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right.

  • You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win.

  • You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one.

  • You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am.

Experience profile:

  • 2+ years of software engineering experience shipping high-quality architectures for critical systems

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals — you write clean, well-tested, production-ready code

  • Hands-on experience with distributed systems at production scale

  • Experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS preferred)

  • Familiarity with observability practices (SLOs, error budgets, alerting, dashboards)

  • Track record of leading technical projects end-to-end, including cross-team coordination

  • Comfortable using AI tooling and coding agents as part of your everyday engineering workflow — we expect our engineers to leverage these tools to move faster and think bigger

Bonus (not required):

  • Experience with cellular or multi-tenant architecture patterns

  • Prior work on workflow orchestration systems (Temporal)

  • Contributions to developer experience or internal platform tooling

  • Experience in fintech, payments, or regulated industries (FedRAMP, SOC 2)

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay

Referral Instructions

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 

Other notices

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp needs a highly organized operator to make immigration and mobility work feel clear, responsive, and scalable. This role will spend roughly half its time coordinating active cases and employee communications in tandem with an external counsel program with embedded services, and half building the workflows, dashboards, AI tools, and operational infrastructure that reduce manual work.

The Associate will operate within established policies, escalate legal or non-standard issues promptly, and streamline operations for scale.

What You'll Do

Case coordination and employee service (~50%)

  • Coordinate active immigration, work-authorization, relocation, and business-travel cases with employees, external counsel, vendors, and internal partners.

  • Maintain accurate case trackers, deadlines, required documents, status updates, and handoffs from intake through completion.

  • Give employees timely, compassionate, plain-language process updates; route legal questions, pathway decisions, and exceptions to counsel or the Lead.

  • Surface cases at risk early and ensure the right owner has a clear next action.

  • Support our external counsel’s embedded services by providing dependable operational support, case updates, and guidance within approved policies.

Workflow, AI, and operations (~50%)

  • Build and maintain centralized workflows, intake forms, templates, knowledge resources, and AI-enabled tools that streamline routine work.

  • Own the immigration and mobility case tracker and dashboard: data quality, reporting, aging cases, key dates, operational metrics, and risk visibility.

  • Turn recurring employee and stakeholder questions into approved self-service content and consistent communication templates.

  • Test and document tools and automations with appropriate privacy, data-quality, and human-escalation controls.

  • Identify recurring friction in cases, handoffs, and vendor interactions; bring specific improvement recommendations to the Lead.

Program and vendor support

  • Prepare case trends, SLA performance, employee feedback, and unresolved risks for vendor/counsel meetings and QBRs.

  • Follow through on vendor commitments and escalate missed deadlines, unclear ownership, and repeat quality issues.

  • Keep playbooks, templates, and operational documentation current; help build team coverage and continuity.

What You Need

  • 3+ years in People Operations, immigration operations, global mobility, employee lifecycle operations, or another high-detail service environment.

  • Strong process-management skills, attention to detail, and proven ability to manage many deadlines without dropping follow-through.

  • Hands-on experience improving a workflow with AI, automation, spreadsheets, dashboards, ticketing, or related tools.

  • Clear, empathetic written communication and sound discretion with sensitive employee information.

  • Comfort working within defined policies, recognizing risk, and escalating promptly.

Nice to Have

  • Experience coordinating immigration, work authorization, relocation, or external counsel/vendor workflows.

  • Experience building employee-facing guides, operational dashboards, or self-service tools.

  • Familiarity with UK, Canada, or broader international employment processes.

Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global)

  • Flexible PTO

  • Centralized home-office equipment ordering

  • Health and wellness stipend

  • Budget for intra-office travel

  • Weekly coffee stipend

United States

  • 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

  • One Medical annual membership

  • 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

  • Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

  • Pet insurance

  • In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

  • Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)

Canada

  • Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

  • Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

  • Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

  • Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

  • Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health

United Kingdom

  • Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

  • Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

  • Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

  • Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay
